placements.why: The repo's strata is empty, and this envelope's entire content — bringing the Kestrelwood spectrograph to a verified operating frequency and confirming it against named reference plates — is calibration-grain organizational content: it names an instrument-readiness record, not a strategy, product, or architecture claim. Nothing in the (empty) supplied strata covers it, and the envelope's own note ('Observatory Calibration: Kestrelwood Spectrograph') names exactly this category, so it is minted standalone with no forced parent.
placements.title: Instrument readiness becomes a standing organizational record rather than a one-off engineering note

placements.title: Calibration is asserted as confirmed against an external standard, not merely set
placements.frame: Does this expression report an instrument's calibration being checked and holding against a named external reference, rather than simply being adjusted or declared?
placements.why: All three segments carry the same recurring thematic content: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration at 88.4 MHz is not just stated but checked against a named external standard (the June reference plates) and found to hold across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes (other instruments, later re-verifications, drift checks) would keep feeding — the grain test's 'true beyond the words it describes' — rather than a single unrepeatable fact, so it earns its own leaf rather than being folded as raw evidence into something else. src-1 carries Quill's direct assertion of the theme; src-2 and src-3 restate the same theme as structured field-labels, differing only in footing, not in topic, so all three ground the same leaf.
